name: Password reset token leaked via Referer
description:
The page behind the password reset link keeps the reset token in its URL and makes a request to another origin with that full URL in the Referer header, because its referrer policy (a Referrer-Policy header or a meta referrer, such as unsafe-url) sends the full URL cross-origin. The third party receives a working reset token for every visit.

burpsy observes this by loading the page in a browser in which every cross-origin request is blocked before it is sent, or, without a browser, computes it from the page's effective policy and its cross-origin subresources.

This row is burpsy's own. Burp's catalogue has the related 'Cross-domain Referer leakage' row, which is a passive heuristic over pages in the site map; the reset page is only reached through the mailed link.
remediation: Serve the reset page with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer (or strict-origin), load no third-party resources on it, and move the token out of the URL (for example into a POST body or a short-lived cookie) once the page has read it.

references.title: OWASP WSTG: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities (WSTG-ATHN-09)
